source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Early septic shock always causes cool skin and increased systemic vascular resistance","B":"Septic and cardiogenic shock produce identical hemodynamic patterns in all patients","C":"Neither septic nor cardiogenic shock produces meaningful skin or perfusion changes","D":"Early septic shock may cause warm skin and reduced systemic vascular resistance"}}
source_row.rationale: In the early ("warm") phase of septic shock, widespread vasodilation from the inflammatory response leads to warm, flushed skin and decreased systemic vascular resistance, contrasting with cardiogenic shock, which typically presents with cool, clammy skin and elevated systemic vascular resistance due to compensatory vasoconstriction in response to poor cardiac output.
source_row.source_detail: Septic shock typically lowers SVR with a hyperdynamic/warm phase; cardiogenic shock lowers output and raises SVR; accessed 2026-08-14.
